aiAdvice.conditions_outgoing:
Condition output is narrow and top-heavy. **Burning and Bleeding account for 76% of all condition damage** (199K and 131K respectively), but neither is stacking efficiently — Burning averages only ~194 damage per application across 1,026 hits, and Bleeding ~101 per application across 1,307 hits. These are low-per-stack numbers, meaning stacks aren't reaching meaningful depth before falling off.

Torment (46K), Poison (26K), and Confusion (14K) are minor contributors. **No utility conditions are being applied** — Chill, Immobilize, Fear, Slow, and Blind are effectively zero across all 57 fights. The squad is outputting pure damage-over-time with zero movement or action control.

Coverage is concentrated in a few sources. Burning ties to Wildfire and Napalm from a small number of fire-damage players. Bleeding and Torment come from the necromancer line (Life Transfer, Well of Suffering, Life Reap). If those players are downed or out of range, condition pressure drops to near zero.
aiAdvice.composition:
The support bench is thin. Only 4 players have support confidence above 50% — three Druids and one Luminary. Those four also account for nearly all healing (top healer 1.16M HPS; fourth drops to 436K) and the majority of cleanses (1,203 of ~1,700 total). Everyone else tagged "support" sits at 0–28% confidence, meaning the roster is effectively 4 healers deep with no reliable second tier.

**Stability coverage is the critical gap.** Organized groups hit 40–62% Stability in clean wins but dropped to 0–8% in the worst losses. Alacrity is 0% across every fight. Might is effectively zero. The squad has no Alacrity or Might generation at all.

**Strips are critically low** — only two damage players produce meaningful strips (267 and 199). The rest of the squad combined produced under 20. Enemy Stability goes uncontested in most engagements.

24–27 PUGs were present per fight, receiving 0% Stability, 0% Quickness, and near-0% Aegis. They are unbooned and dying accordingly, but they are not in voice and not coachable.

The roster can win clean fights when boons land. It cannot sustain through condition-heavy engagements with 4 healers, no Alacrity, negligible Might, and almost no strips.
aiAdvice.spike_damage:
Spike damage is real but it's not converting to kills. The top burst players hit 12K–17K peak singles and 40K–70K in 1-second windows — strong numbers. But the squad's overall kill:down ratio sits at **0.6:1**, meaning burst lands without finishing targets.

**The strip gap is why.** Only two players produce meaningful boon strips (267 and 199 total across 57 fights). Enemy Stability goes largely uncontested, so burst damage hits into protected targets that don't down. In the Askalion Hills 7:34 fight — the squad's best sustained engagement — 38 squad downs produced 43 enemy kills (1.2:1), the only fight where the ratio broke positive at scale. That fight also had organized-group Stability at 48–62%.

Contrast that with the Orchard Overlook wipe: 28 squad downs, 24 deaths, only 4 enemy kills (0.1:1). Squad Stability was 2% with Resistance at 0%. The burst was there, but without strips to drop enemy Stability and without our own Stability to survive the counter-bomb, spikes hit into unbroken targets and the squad fed.

**Bottom line:** burst output is sufficient. The conversion problem is upstream — strips and Stability, not damage.
aiAdvice.damage_breakdown:
**Squad damage is carried by 4 skills. The top 4 outgoing skills account for over 1.36M damage — roughly 40% of total output.** Overload Air alone did 510K across 492 hits. Life Transfer, Soul Spiral, and Well of Suffering round out the core.

**Burst skills are underused.** Offensive Protocol: Obliterate — the squad's hardest single-hit skill (17K peak) — was cast only 61 times across 57 fights. That's barely one cast per fight. Flame Blast (86 casts) and Life Reap (65 casts) show the same pattern: high-impact, low-frequency.

**Sustained AoE is doing the heavy lifting.** Burning (1,721 hits), Soul Spiral (646 hits), and Life Transfer (691 hits) are spam-density skills. They pad total damage but don't convert downs — their down-contribution per hit is low.

**The spike gap is massive.** Top burst players hit 47K-70K in 1-second windows. The bottom half of the roster peaked under 10K in 1s. Those players are not contributing burst during bombs — they're along for the ride.

**Bottom line:** The squad wins on AoE volume, not burst execution. When fights require quick target deletion — outnumbered engages, picking off isolated enemies — the burst rotation isn't there. More frequent use of hard-hitting skills during the bomb window, not more total damage, is what's missing.
aiAdvice.mitigation:
Mitigation correlates directly with survival. The top mitigators — the Firebrands and Troubadours blocking 70+ times each — took 767K and 519K damage respectively but only died twice. One Firebrand blocked 70 times for 221K mitigated and survived every fight with zero deaths.

The flip side: the one Amalgam with only 3 evades and 3 blocks mitigated just 16K total and died 4 times on only 86K damage taken. That player ate damage raw — low mitigation, high death count, low total intake. They are not dodging or blocking during bombs.

The Necromancer is the standout — 58 evades, 39 blocks, 150K mitigated, only 1 death on 496K taken. Active dodging kept them alive despite heavy intake.

**Pattern**: players who block and evade actively survive even when taking 500K+ damage. Players who don't mitigate die on a fraction of the intake. The melee players with low block counts need to use defensive cooldowns during enemy bombs, not just during their own.
aiAdvice.boon_strips:
**Boon strip output is a critical single point of failure.** Two players produced 1,370 and 849 strips — over 60% of the squad's total. The next tier (Spellbreaker 834, Scourge 817, Reaper 791) brings the core to five players carrying essentially all strip pressure.

Everyone else combined produced under 30 strips across 57 fights. The healers and boon providers — who should be contributing passive strips — generated 0–16 each.

**Impact**: When any of those top five strip players are downed, dead, or out of range, enemy Stability goes uncontested. This directly explains the 0.6:1 kill:down ratio — enemies keep Stability through bombs, avoid CC, and win the downstate race.

**Fix**: Every player with access to boon-strip skills needs to use them on cooldown during engages. Strip pressure must be distributed, not concentrated in five players.
aiAdvice.boons:
**Stability is the single biggest issue in this raid.** Squad-average uptime never exceeded 22%, and one fight hit 0% across every group. When organized groups held Stability above 40%, the squad took zero deaths. Below 12%, we wiped.

- **Stability**: Squad average 0–22%. Best organized groups peaked at 59–62%. PUGs sat at 0% every fight.
- **Quickness**: Squad average 1–23%. Best groups hit 35–58% in clean wins. Too low for consistent damage output.
- **Resistance**: Squad average 0–13%. Enemy condi damage (Burning, Wildfire) was the top incoming source. This gap directly fed deaths.
- **Might**: Effectively zero. Top value on the leaderboard was 1.
- **Alacrity**: 0% in every fight.
- **Regeneration**: The one bright spot — 40–55% squad average, organized groups hitting 77–99%. Druids carried this.

**Stability sources**: The leaderboard shows zero meaningful generation from any player. Firebrands, Chronomancers, Troubadours, and the Luminary all registered 0. The uptime that did appear came from transient sources, not sustained rotation.

**Bottom line**: No Stability during engages means the squad gets CC'd, can't bomb, and dies. This is the #1 fix before the next raid.
aiAdvice.boon_timeline:
**Stability gaps are the single strongest predictor of squad deaths this raid.**

The Askalion Hills win at 0:54 saw total Stability collapse — every organized group at 0%, Aegis at 0%, Resistance at 0%. That fight still came out clean (0 deaths, 8 kills) but only because the enemy was 28 players on a 22-player squad with no real pressure.

The Orchard Overlook loss tells the real story. Stability sat at 8% squad-wide, organized groups managed only 20-31%, and 20 players died with 1 enemy kill. The Askalion Hills 0:49 loss was worse — 25 deaths, 0 kills, and multiple groups had 0% Stability during the engage.

**Contrast with the fights that worked.** The Askalion Hills 7:35 win — 23v83, 21 deaths but 43 kills — had organized groups holding 55% and 26% Stability. The clean Askalion Hills 1:07 win had groups at 54% and 48%. When organized groups hold above 40% Stability, the squad trades favorably or takes zero deaths.

**The pattern is clear:** Stability drops below 20% squad-wide, deaths cluster immediately. Resistance tracks the same curve — near 0% in every loss fight, and the enemy is hitting with heavy Burning and fire damage. The squad's boon providers are not maintaining uptime during engages, and the death count follows directly.
aiAdvice.stab_performance:
**Stability gaps are the single strongest predictor of squad deaths this raid.**

In the Orchard Overlook loss, squad Stability averaged just 8% — organized groups peaked at 31%, multiple groups sat at 0%. That fight produced 20 squad deaths for 1 enemy kill. In the Askalion Hills clean wins, organized groups held Stability above 50% and took zero deaths.

The pattern is consistent: when organized-group Stability drops below 35%, the squad wipes. When it holds above 50%, the squad trades favorably.

**Far-from-tag players are dying during stab drops.** Several players have p95 distances exceeding 12,000 units — well outside any boon radius. These players receive 0% Stability, 0% Aegis, and 0% Quickness. They are unbooned and isolated when the enemy bombs.

- Players with p95 distances above 12K units are the same players showing 0% Stability uptime in boon breakdowns.
- PUGs received 0% Stability across every fight with boon data. They are not in voice and cannot be coached, but their deaths inflate the squad's downstate race deficit.

**Fix:** Collapse tighter on tag before engages. Stability coverage falls off sharply past ~300 units. Players at 500+ median distance are in the boon gap and will die first.
aiAdvice.support:
**Support output has two critical gaps: stripping and cleanse throughput.**

- **Strips are almost nonexistent.** Two damage players produced 466 strips combined. The rest of the squad — including all support players — produced **under 15 strips total across 57 fights**. Enemy Stability goes uncontested every engage.
- **Cleanses are thin against condition pressure.** The top three healers produced ~1,000 cleanses combined, but Burning alone was applied **1,026 times**. Spread across 57 fights, the squad is cleansing roughly **20 conditions per fight** — not enough against condi-heavy enemy comps.
- **Healing is a four-player bench.** Three healers output 800K–1.16M each. The next tier drops to 180K. Losing any healer to death or positioning breaks the healing chain — and the loss fights confirm healers among the dead.
- **Resurrects are minimal** (max 5 per player across the entire raid), consistent with zero rallies observed. The squad is not recovering downs through rezzes.

The strip gap is the most actionable. Until the squad can remove enemy Stability, bombs won't convert to kills.
aiAdvice.healing:
Healing is concentrated in four players and the bench drops off a cliff after that. The top three healers combined for 3.1M healing at ~1,100 HPS each. The fourth healer produced 436K — less than 40% of the others. Everyone else is under 180K total.

**The coverage gap is the problem.** With only four meaningful healers, losing any one to death or positioning breaks the chain. Two of the top three healers died during the raid — when they go down, there is no backup.

**Positioning is compounding it.** Two healers have p95 distances over 7,500 units from tag. At those ranges they are outside Stability, Aegis, and cleanse radius — they cannot heal the melee ball and the melee ball cannot protect them. Median distances are fine (~200-260 units), meaning healers are in position most of the time but regularly wander far enough to break coverage.

**Healing vs damage taken doesn't add up.** The top damage-takers absorbed 490K-767K each. Four healers at ~1,100 HPS cannot cover that spread across a 15-25 player squad during a bomb. The squad needs healers tighter on tag and the fifth/sixth healers contributing more than 180K.
aiAdvice.incoming_damage:
The squad is dying to fire condition pressure. **Burning** alone dealt 454K damage across 1,619 hits — more than any other source. **Fire Cannon** added 353K, and **Wildfire** contributed 244K.

That's over 1M damage from fire-themed sources. The counter-play is Resistance and cleanses. Squad Resistance averaged 0-13% across fights. In the Green Alpine Borderlands engagements, it never exceeded 13% squad-wide.

Cleanse output ran roughly 30 per fight across 57 fights. Against 1,619 Burning applications alone, that's nowhere near enough.

**The fix is boon timing, not comp changes.** Resistance and Resolution must be pre-cast before enemy bombs land, not reactively. The squad's healers are keeping Regen up (40-55%) but are not covering the condition damage window.
aiAdvice.push_timing:
The squad is consistently pushing dry. Every major loss shows organized-group Stability below 8%, and the worst wipes had **0% Stability across all groups**. Meanwhile, clean wins hit 50-62% Stability in organized groups.

The pattern is clear: when the squad pushed with boons, it took zero deaths. When it pushed without them, it wiped.

- **0% Stability, 0% Aegis, 0% Resistance** — the squad's boon providers generated nothing during multiple full-wipe fights. All organized groups sat at zero. The squad pushed into enemy bombs with no protection layer at all.
- **Clean wins correlate directly with Stability above 40%.** The fights where organized groups hit 50-62% Stability produced zero squad deaths. The fights where they sat at 0-8% produced 12-25 deaths.
- **Strips are nearly nonexistent.** Only 2 players produced meaningful strip output (267 and 199 across 57 fights). Enemy Stability was uncontested on every push — the squad bombed into enemies who had stab, while having none of its own.
- **Quickness followed the same curve.** Clean wins saw 35-58% Quickness in organized groups. Wipe fights saw 0-4%. The squad was pushing with slow skill activation into enemies who were not slowed.

**Bottom line:** The squad is not waiting for boon windows before engaging. Pushes are happening dry — no Stability, no Quickness, no Aegis — into enemies whose Stability is never stripped. Every clean win had boons up. Every wipe had boons down. Fix the push timing: wait for the Stability cast, then go.
aiAdvice.positioning:
Squad cohesion is not the problem. Median distance to tag sits at 200-350 units for most players — tight enough to bomb and within heal range. The squad was stacked correctly during engages.

**The losses are execution and boon state, not positioning.** The Orchard Overlook and Greenlake wipes show 12-19 deaths with 0-1 kills despite the squad being collapsed on tag. When the squad is tight but still wipes, the issue is Stability uptime (0-8% in those fights) and near-zero Resistance against heavy incoming condition pressure.

A few players have extreme p95 distance spikes (12,000-29,000 units), but those are outlier moments — likely respawns or map transit — not the cause of fight losses. The deaths happened inside the bomb, not out of position.

**Bottom line:** Stop chasing positioning as the fix. The squad stacks correctly. The problem is that organized groups are bombing with under 12% Stability and near-0% Resistance. Fix the boon gaps first.
aiAdvice.offense:
Damage is carried by four players. The top four damage dealers produced 6.3M combined — everyone else is under 4.3M, and the bottom half of the roster sits below 100K total. That's not a deep bench; it's a cliff.

**The burst rotation isn't firing.** Hard-hitting skills like Offensive Protocol: Obliterate were cast roughly once per fight across 57 fights. The squad wins on AoE volume — Overload Air, Life Transfer, Soul Spiral — not on target deletion. When fights require quick kills, the burst isn't there.

**Strips are the bottleneck.** Only two players produce meaningful boon strips (267 and 199 total). Enemy Stability goes uncontested, so burst hits into protected targets that don't down. The kill:down ratio sits at 0.6:1 — damage lands, targets survive.

**Bottom line:** raw output is fine. The conversion problem is upstream. Without strips to break enemy Stability, damage doesn't translate to kills.
aiAdvice.defense:
**Deaths cluster in fights where the downstate trade collapses entirely.** The Greenlake loss produced 19 deaths and 25 downs for 1 enemy kill — a 0.0:1 kill:down ratio. Orchard Overlook and Askalion Hills losses followed the same pattern: 20-25 squad deaths, 0-1 enemy kills, zero rallies.

**Zero rallies across all 57 fights.** Every down either gets revived or dies — no one is trading deaths to save downed players. The squad is losing the downstate race because enemies keep Stability through bombs (strips are concentrated in two players) and the squad doesn't.

**The death count tracks Stability directly.** Clean wins had organized groups above 40% Stability and zero deaths. Every wipe had squad Stability under 12%. The Greenlake and Orchard Overlook losses are the clearest examples — low Stability, high condition intake (Burning was the top incoming source), and no Resistance to counter it.

**Mitigation separates survivors from casualties.** Players who blocked 70+ times survived every fight. Players with under 5 blocks and 3 evades died repeatedly on less damage taken. Active defensive cooldowns during enemy bombs are the difference between a down and a death.
aiAdvice.commander_stats:
The commander died 8 times across 57 fights. That's low — the tag stayed up in most engagements. But the **83% collapse rate** is the real problem.

When the tag went down, the squad folded 83% of the time. That's not a tag-survivability issue. It's a **squad-discipline issue**. The squad is entirely dependent on the commander being alive to hold formation. Once the tag drops, there's no secondary call, no fallback anchor — the squad disintegrates.

The **0.6:1 kill:down ratio** confirms this. The squad downs enemies but can't finish them. 159 failed downs across the raid means the squad is getting people down but not converting — because the push stalls, the tag dies, and the squad collapses before it can stomp.

The push timing issue compounds this. Dry pushes with 0% Stability mean the tag is absorbing the first CC wave. When the tag goes down in a dry push, the squad has no boons to fall back on and no one calling the regroup.

**Fix:** Designate a secondary caller before the raid. When the tag drops, the secondary needs to call "regroup on me" immediately — not wait for the tag to respawn. The squad needs a fallback anchor point, not just the tag.
aiAdvice.squad_stats:
**Damage is concentrated in 3 players.** The top 3 damage dealers produced 4.3M combined — 65% of the squad's total. Everyone else is under 500K. Kill pressure comes almost entirely from Overload Air, Life Transfer, and Soul Spiral. When those players are downed or out of range, the squad has no bomb.

**Incoming damage is condition-dominant.** Burning alone dealt 454K across 1,619 hits — more than the squad's top single skill. The enemy is out-damaging us in the condition war while we lack the Resistance and cleanses to survive it.

**Tag distance is fine during engages.** Median distance sits at 200-400 units for most players. The squad stacks correctly. The p95 spikes (12K-29K) are respawn/transit noise, not fight deaths.

**PUGs are dying unbooned.** PUGs sit at 0% Stability, 0% Quickness, 0% Aegis in nearly every fight. They are not in voice and cannot be coached, but their deaths inflate the body count and feed enemy rallies.
aiAdvice.fight_overview:
43 wins, 14 losses across 57 fights — a 75% win rate that masks a stark split. The squad rolled small groups and paper objectives cleanly, with 30+ fights at zero squad deaths. Every loss followed the same pattern: outnumbered, 12–25 squad deaths, 0–1 enemy kills.

**The biggest swing fight was the 7:34 Askalion Hills engagement.** 23 players into an 83-enemy force, 21 squad deaths — but 43 enemy kills and a 2.0 K/D. That fight proved the squad can trade into superior numbers when boons land and burst connects. The problem is consistency: the same squad produced 25 deaths and zero kills in the 0:49 Askalion Hills wipe. The difference wasn't the enemy — it was Stability uptime and strip output.
